Need To Know
Mississippi Race Set
The Associated Press
called Mississippi's Senate race
for Scott Colom (D) yesterday after counties updated their results amid ballot review and processing. The latest tally puts Colom ahead of incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) by over 4,600 votes, or roughly 0.5% of the total. Hyde-Smith has conceded.
Colom will become the state's first Black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Mississippi was the first state to send a Black senator to Congress, with Sen.
Hiram Revels
(R-MS) serving from 1870 to 1871. Sen.
Blanche Bruce
(R-MS) served from 1875 to 1881. No Black senators have been elected from the state in the years since, though Mississippi boasts the largest proportion of Black residents of any state (37.9%). Colom's victory also marks the first Democratic senator elected from Mississippi in over 40 years.
Democrats were
late to inject cash
into the race, with Mississippi not widely considered a pickup opportunity. One viral ad campaign by Colom centered on Hyde-Smith's comments on the price of beef; watch it
here
(via YouTube).
Alaska is the last remaining Senate race to be called as of this writing, alongside a dozen House races. See live updates
here
Russia-Ukraine Talks Wrap
Russia and Ukraine
agreed in principle
to a large prisoner-of-war exchange yesterday after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a major breakthrough toward ending the nearly five-year war.
The exchange could occur within two to three weeks, with the number of prisoners to be finalized today (how the countries
exchange POWs
). The talks marked the countries' first direct negotiations in nine months, with disagreements remaining over Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory and postwar security guarantees. European officials were excluded at
Moscow’s insistence
but consulted with Ukraine’s delegation on the sidelines. The Kremlin opposes Europe's military and financial support for Ukraine, while Ukraine wants its European allies involved. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow today before meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin.
The war has displaced nearly 10 million Ukrainians and become Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II. Track the conflict on an interactive map
here

The Coachella Economy
Pop star Dua Lipa, psychedelic pop act Tame Impala, and R&B artist SZA
will headline
the 2027 Coachella music festival, organizers revealed yesterday. See the full
lineup
here
Since its 1999
debut, Coachella has evolved into a major pop culture tastemaker. (It wasn't an overnight success;
read history
.) The 2026 festival drew roughly 125,000 daily attendees, with weekend passes starting around $600. The
rise of festival-going
reflects the growing appeal of the experience economy, with two-thirds of 18- to 35-year-olds saying they'd
rather attend a live event
than buy a product of a similar value. Musicians are also increasingly relying on live music revenue as album sales fall and digital streaming payouts remain low. Headliners can command up to $5M per weekend, while smaller artists reportedly earn closer to $10K.
The new Coachella lineup signals a potential revival of late-2000s and early-2010s dance music, with performances from Madonna, Robyn, and more. Why is Gen Z embracing
recession pop
? (w/audio)
